title: The Late Harbor
premise: Jude Underhill ghostwrites memoirs for the famous, invisible by trade and choice, until his latest client turns out to be the estranged half-brother of Wren Calloway, the vineyard events planner who once shared a perfect, unfinished summer with him. When Wren needs a fake date to survive her family's reunion, Jude agrees, hiding both his identity and the memoir that will expose her family's oldest wound. As the reunion curdles into scandal and the harvest approaches, Jude must choose between the career that keeps him safe and the woman who makes him want to be seen, finally confessing who he is and what he's written. He loses her trust, then wins it back by burning his contract and telling the truth in his own name, staying through the first harvest as the last train of the season pulls away without him.
about_author: A. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former wine-country event coordinator who spent a decade watching strangers fall in love at other people's weddings. They write romance about people who are better at keeping secrets than keeping promises.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He delivers a finished memoir to a celebrity who can't remember his name, establishing his invisible life and his rule against attachments. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His agent offers a lucrative contract: the memoir of Marcus Vane, self-made vintner. The source material mentions a family in Harbor Bluffs, and a name Jude recognizes. Emotional beat: dread beneath ambition.

chapters.title: Last Train to Harbor Bluffs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He returns to the coastal town he fled twelve years ago for research and runs, literally, into Wren Calloway at the station. Neither lets on they know each other. Emotional beat: the past arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: A Favor Between Strangers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Desperate to avoid her family's pity over her broken engagement, Wren asks the familiar-looking stranger to be her date to the reunion. Jude agrees before he can think. Emotional beat: recklessness as self-rescue.

chapters.title: The Rules of Pretending
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. They negotiate fake-dating terms over cheap wine: no real names in public, no real feelings ever. Both are already lying about something bigger. Emotional beat: complicity disguised as caution.

chapters.title: Reunion, Act One
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Calloway estate reunion begins; Wren's grandmother scrutinizes Jude, and Marcus Vane's arrival as a family investor stuns the room. Emotional beat: performance under pressure.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wren's grandmother corners him; to protect Wren, he improvises a story about how they met, and it's the true one, from the summer they actually shared. Wren goes still. Emotional beat: the fake cracking.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She confronts Jude privately; he admits only that he knew her years ago, not why he left or who he's working for. She chooses not to push. Emotional beat: hunger for truth, fear of it.

chapters.title: The Client's Manuscript
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Back in his rented cottage, he reads Vane's draft and finds the chapter describing the Calloway family secret: the debt, the fire, the death Wren's family covered up. Emotional beat: the weight of other people's truths.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pre-harvest preparations begin; Jude volunteers to help, clumsy but earnest, and the crew adopts him. Wren watches him fit in and hates how much she wants that to be real. Emotional beat: belonging, tested.

chapters.title: Twelve Summers Ago
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, flashback. The summer he and Wren were nineteen: the promise to leave together, his father's collapse, the train he took alone. Emotional beat: guilt as origin story.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grandmother Calloway, sharp as ever, warns Wren that Jude is hiding something, and reveals she knows Vane is writing a book. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Interviews and Innuendo
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He interviews Vane on-site, forced to transcribe the man's casual cruelty about the Calloways while Wren works nearby. Emotional beat: complicity turning to shame.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm damages the vines a week before harvest; the community rallies, and Jude works through the night beside Wren. Soaked and laughing, they almost kiss. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The almost-kiss haunts him. He drafts an email to his agent quitting the Vane book, then deletes it, needing the money and the mask. Emotional beat: cowardice with good reasons.

chapters.title: Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Vane, charming and wounded, confides in Jude about his exile from the family and his hunger for vindication, making the betrayal feel almost righteous. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Family Tree
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Vane is her father's half-brother, erased after the fire that killed their grandfather, and realizes the reunion is his stage for revenge. Emotional beat: the past is a living relative.

chapters.title: Date Number Six
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A real date disguised as a fake one: the harbor fair, fried dough, a fortune teller who tells Jude the truth he's avoiding. They kiss for the crowd, then again for no one. Emotional beat: falling, knowingly.

chapters.title: The Draft Leaks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A partial manuscript page surfaces, photographed at Vane's rented office, hinting the Calloways' patriarch died in a fire they set to collect insurance. Wren sees it first. Emotional beat: the secret escaping its cage.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Breakfast
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The family fractures; Grandmother Calloway interrogates everyone, and Wren realizes Jude arrived the same week the book began. Suspicion blooms. Emotional beat: love and doubt in the same mouth.

chapters.title: The Question She Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wren asks what he does for a living; he says 'consulting.' She lets it go, and her letting it go feels worse than an accusation. Emotional beat: the cost of a spared question.

chapters.title: Vane Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Vane presents the family an ultimatum: acknowledge him and the truth, or he publishes everything. He names Jude as his biographer in front of them all. Emotional beat: betrayal detonating in daylight.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, humiliated, tells Jude to leave on the evening train. He boards it. She watches it go and tells herself it's what she wanted. Emotional beat: the ending that isn't one.

chapters.title: What Jude Wrote
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, on the train and after. He reads his own manuscript and realizes he wrote Vane's story to avoid writing his own, and Wren's, and his father's. Emotional beat: the ghostwriter haunted.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Harvest prep stalls; the crew misses Jude; Wren finds the notebook he left behind with notes for a different book, one about her family told with tenderness instead of venom. Emotional beat: evidence of care.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grandmother Calloway admits the fire's truth: her husband's greed, the death, the silence that broke the family. She gives Wren the choice she never had. Emotional beat: inheritance of guilt, offered honestly.

chapters.title: The Agent's Call
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His agent offers to kill the Vane book if Jude delivers a juicier one: the Calloway scandal in his own byline. Fame, finally, at exactly the wrong price. Emotional beat: temptation wearing his own name.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Draft
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He writes through the night: a full confession chapter, naming himself, his father's debt, the summer he abandoned, and what Vane's memoir would have done to Wren. Emotional beat: authorship as atonement.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The first harvest begins at dawn without resolution; Wren decides that whatever Jude did, she'll face the family's truth publicly before Vane can weaponize it. Emotional beat: courage as inheritance.

chapters.title: Vane's Press Conference
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Vane goes public, excerpts leak, and the Calloway name trends; Wren watches her family's history get narrated by a stranger. Emotional beat: violation by headline.

chapters.title: The Counter-Story
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren gives her own interview, telling the fire's truth on the family's terms, with grief instead of accusation. The town's response is complicated, but hers. Emotional beat: reclaiming the narrative.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Mail
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude sends Wren his full confession chapter and terminates the Vane contract, eating the penalty that will bankrupt him. Emotional beat: ruin chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Return Platform
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Jude arrives back in Harbor Bluffs with no contract, no money, and one printed chapter. Wren meets him at the station and doesn't speak. Emotional beat: hope with no safety net.

chapters.title: What He Should Have Said
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude reads the confession aloud to Wren in the empty tasting room: the summer, the leaving, the book, all of it. She listens without mercy or absolution. Emotional beat: truth without negotiation.

chapters.title: The Family Vote
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Calloways convene; Grandmother Calloway, to everyone's shock, sides with Wren: publish the truth themselves, in a book Jude will write, credited to him by name. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy.

chapters.title: First Pick
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The first harvest comes in; Jude works the rows beside Wren, hands stained, name spoken freely. Vane, watching his leverage dissolve, is offered a seat at the table instead of a war. Emotional beat: harvest as homecoming.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Offered acknowledgment instead of revenge, Vane wavers, then accepts a chapter in the family's book, his exile ending not with victory but with a chair pulled out for him. Emotional beat: the antagonist's grace.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Calloway book is announced with Jude Underhill's name on the cover, his first. His old clients call; he lets the calls go to voicemail. Emotional beat: visibility as arrival.

chapters.title: The Last Train of the Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The season's final train pulls out of Harbor Bluffs; Jude, who once left on it, stands on the platform and lets it go without him. Wren takes his hand. Emotional beat: staying as the love story.

chapters.title: First Bottling
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing. Spring: the first bottles of the truth-told vintage are labeled, the book is finished, and Wren asks Jude what he'll write next. 'Us,' he says, and this time it isn't fiction. Emotional beat: belonging, earned.
